# Distributed Wearable Human Activity Recognition

Welcome to the technical documentation of the **HAR Distributed Framework**, a distributed wearable computing system developed for Real-Time Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using embedded computing devices and wearable inertial sensors.

This website documents the design, implementation, configuration, deployment, and experimental evaluation of the complete framework.

The main purpose of this documentation is to provide the technical information required to understand **how the system was built** and to facilitate its reproduction, extension, and adaptation for future research.

## What is documented here?

The documentation covers the complete development workflow of the system, including:

- Wearable Sensing and Data Acquisition
- Embedded Computing Infrastructure
- Dataset Preparation and Preprocessing
- Local Neural Network Development
- Distributed Inference
- Probability-Level Communication
- Multi-Node Synchronization
- Central Prediction Fusion
- Real-Time Deployment
- System Monitoring and Logging
- Graphical Visualization
- Experimental Evaluation
- Centralized And Distributed Configurations
- Robustness Experiments
- Result Reproduction

## Framework at a Glance

The system follows a distributed inference architecture in which wearable sensor data are processed close to their source using embedded edge devices. Each edge device executes a local Human Activity Recognition model and transmits class probability vectors rather than continuous raw sensor streams. These predictions are collected by a central node, synchronized, and combined to produce the final global activity prediction.
